answer: Constraint-Satisfaction Fingerprinting. Each agent must satisfy a randomly drawn constraint set (e.g., prove co-presence in a meadow simulation, respond to a gale event, cross-reference ocean data), and the draws are seeded per epoch. Colluders can't precompute answers, so every identity pays a fresh solve and coordination cost each round. Detection runs after the fact: clusters whose constraint solutions are suspiciously correlated or reuse latent strategy get flagged and slashed. Attacker cost scales with live per-identity compute plus coordination, not one-time registration.
